reason: The five lines and their breaks match the Hirshfield and Aratani text exactly, checked against the Tricycle printing that carries the publisher’s full credit: ‘From The Ink Dark Moon: Love Poems by Ono No Komachi and Izumi Shikibu, Women of the Ancient Court of Japan, translated by Jane Hirshfield with Mariko Aratani. Published by Vintage Books. Translation copyright 1986, 1987, 1988, 1989, 1990 by Jane Hirshfield.’ Line by line: Although the wind / blows terribly here, / the moonlight also leaks / between the roof planks / of this ruined house. Comma after ‘here’, full stop after ‘house’, lower case at every line head after the first, all as the card prints them. The correction the verifier already made is right and I confirmed it independently: the copyright page of the paperback reads FIRST VINTAGE CLASSICS EDITION, OCTOBER 1990, and the University of Arizona Voca bibliography cites the first edition as Charles Scribner’s Sons, 1988, so the translation is 1988 and the wording quoted is the Vintage 1990 issue the source now names. The note’s claim about the 1986 to 1990 copyright span is accurate to the credit line. Attribution is right: Tricycle and the Poetry Foundation both file this tanka under Izumi Shikibu, not Ono no Komachi, which is the obvious trap in a two-poet volume and the one I looked for. The tanka is untitled so a first-line locator is the correct form. Not shipped, not near anything shipped, Izumi Shikibu at zero of three, not banned, no other May proposal uses her. In scope, publishable, ends in a full stop, curly punctuation throughout, source line 132 characters and leads with the name. Tag Poetry is the form. Two small things short of a refutation. The evidence field says ‘Vintage Classics, 1990’ while the source line says ‘Vintage, 1990’; the copyright page says Vintage Classics and the credit line says Vintage Books, so either is defensible and the source line is fine as it stands. And this is the weakest of the four on May’s theme: it is an image of consolation rather than counsel or a maxim, so it leans on the curator’s reading that the gaps letting the cold in are the ones letting the light in. That is an editorial call for the board, not a citation break.
